newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips lively, SAX index up 0.46 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips lively, SAX index up 0.46 pts.

text.p: Slovak shares opened the week on Monday slightly higher in lively activity on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE), pushing the SAX index up 0.46 points to 201.13.

Some brokers were optimistic that the market might revive before the end of the year, with both domestic and foreign investors' interest piqued by relatively cheaper valuations than in neighbouring markets.
"Slovak shares are much cheaper at the moment than for example neighbouring Czech market, which might attract some foreign players," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta dominated floor trading, but closed unchanged at 1,900 crowns, though its average price was some 1.21 percent higher.
"Block settlement of 6,000 shares was made in Nafta at 1,925 crowns, but I think the closer of 1,900 is more realistic price, even for larger stakes," Sykora said.
Oil refinery Slovnaft closed unchanged at 900 crowns, while bank VUB increased 20 crowns to 1,760 crowns and steel maker VSZ, one of the most liquid BSE issues, lost five at 625 crowns.
Overall volume increased to 1.034,245 shares, from 464,142 shares traded on Friday, while turnover fell to 377.61 million crowns, from 667.77 million.
